spec_notes: Three 4x4 client-serving radios, 12 total streams. Published 7.78 Gbps is aggregate chipset frame rate, not client throughput. 802.3bt enables USB (30.5W maximum); 802.3at supports all three 4x4 radios and 5G Ethernet with USB disabled. Choose Meraki cloud or Catalyst controller operation; management migration has software requirements.

Built-in directional antennas, not external antennas. Three 4x4 serving radios; 12 total streams. OEM aggregate chipset frame rate is 7.78 Gbps. 802.3bt enables USB; 802.3at operates all three 4x4 radios at 5G Ethernet with USB disabled. 6 GHz operation depends on regional regulation.

Three 4x4 client radios; OEM advertises up to 18 Gbps aggregate chipset frame rate. Single 10G mGig Ethernet, not dual 5G. Full-power operation requires 802.3bt (39W maximum); 802.3at/af use low-power modes. MLO, channel widths, and 6 GHz availability depend on software, client, and regulatory domain.

Internal directional antenna version, intended for high ceilings and large open spaces. Three 4x4 serving radios, 12 aggregate streams, and an OEM-advertised 18 Gbps aggregate chipset frame rate. Single 10G mGig Ethernet. 802.3bt required for full-power features; at/af are low-power modes.

Two client-serving 4x4 radios (eight total streams), plus dedicated scanning and BLE radios. No 6 GHz radio. 2.98 Gbps is the OEM-advertised aggregate chipset frame rate, not client throughput. 802.3at is required; 30W maximum published consumption. Requires Meraki licensing.

Three client-serving 4x4 radios (12 total streams) and dual 5G Ethernet. 7.78 Gbps is the advertised aggregate chipset frame rate. Full feature power uses 802.3bt, up to 40W; minimum 30W PoE+ operation disables USB. A second uplink is not a guarantee of twice the application throughput.

AP-635 has 2x2:2 radios, not 4x4:4: six total client-serving streams. OEM advertises 3.9 Gbps aggregate peak data rate. Dual 2.5G Smart Rate ports. 802.3at operation may restrict USB; Intelligent Power Monitoring and enabled features affect power restrictions. Management mode depends on ArubaOS/AOS version and licensing.

Three 4x4 client-serving radios with 12 aggregate streams. 7.8 Gbps is the rounded OEM aggregate peak data rate, not a single-client rate. Dual 5G Smart Rate Ethernet. 802.3bt is the unrestricted single-source power mode; 802.3at restrictions depend on power management. Management depends on software and licensing.

This is the 831F, not the 431F. OEM publishes up to 5.95 Gbps Wi-Fi 6 PHY rate. 2.4 GHz uses 4x4 and 5 GHz uses 8x8 (or split 4x4+4x4); 12 total serving streams. Includes a dedicated scanning radio and BLE. 5G Ethernet plus a separate 1G port. Full function supports dual 802.3at/bt inputs; single 802.3at disables USB. OEM lists 33W maximum power. FortiGate controller or compatible Fortinet cloud management requires supported firmware and licensing.
